# Harcourt

## Overview

- **Age:** 11  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER V. Nell’s History P11](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0011)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Nell-girl  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER XXV. Obed Insists on Puffed Sleeves P43](../source/v01-c25.md#nw-v01-c25-p0043), [v1 CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream P16](../source/v01-c36.md#nw-v01-c36-p0016)</sub>
- **Role:** teacher at Harborough High School  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER V. Nell’s History P11](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0011)</sub>
- **Origin:** Harborough, Nova Scotia  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER V. Nell’s History P11](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0011)</sub>
- **Status:** alive  _(assumed)_
- **Titles:** Miss Harcourt  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P46](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0046)</sub>

## Appearance

Harcourt is a red-haired girl distinguished by a lengthy crimson plait. She possesses large, sweet eyes, a sweet expression to her lips, and a small pointed chin.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P32](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0032), [v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P33](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0033), [v1 CHAPTER XXIX. An Epoch in Nell’s Life P31](../source/v01-c29.md#nw-v01-c29-p0031)_

## Personality

Ann Harcourt is known for having an extremely poor temper. Because of this, she is required to learn how to control her temper.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P46](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0046)_

## Quotes

> "I could assist you so greatly at present and save you effort in numerous manners. For that single reason, I could truly desire to have been one."
>
> — Harcourt — [v1 CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream P40](../source/v01-c36.md#nw-v01-c36-p0040)

> "Oh, Obed and Thirza are going to be so happy! I have to send a letter with the news to my family immediately."
>
> — Harcourt — [v1 CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream P10](../source/v01-c36.md#nw-v01-c36-p0010)

> "Well, another expectation has been shattered. ‘My life is a perfect graveyard of buried hopes.’ Having come across that line in a book one time, I repeat it to console myself each time I face disappointment about something."
>
> — Harcourt — [v1 CHAPTER V. Nell’s History P3](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0003)

> “Oh, the things I know regarding myself are not actually worth mentioning,” Nell stated with enthusiasm. “Should you merely allow me to describe my self-imagined ideas, you will find it far more fascinating.”
>
> — Harcourt — [v1 CHAPTER V. Nell’s History P9](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0009)

> “I feared it could be the home of Mrs. Tranter,” Nell stated sorrowfully. “Reaching that destination is something I wish to avoid. In a way, it will feel as though all things have come to a close.”
>
> — Harcourt — [v1 CHAPTER V. Nell’s History P26](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0026)
